findings.title: New .gbg/-containment grep-scoping guard swept into 2 of ~9 workflow scripts that need it
locations: instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/dismissals.js:38 (left behind, edited in this same diff)
instruments/audit-changes/workflow/audit.js:71 (left behind, edited in this same diff)
findings.before: hunt.js (base): "Read the source. Follow the data. Ask, of each thing you read, what would have to be true for it to be correct, and then check whether it is." — no grep-scoping guidance anywhere in the sibling scripts either.
findings.after: hunt.js (head): "Nothing under `.gbg/` or `~/.gbg/` is yours to open but the files this prompt names; scope every grep with `--glob '!.gbg/**'`."; panel.js (head) adds the identical "scope every search with `--glob '!.gbg/**'`" to its git/grep grant. Every other workflow script that grants the same broad Bash/Read access over the repo tree — including two others touched in this very diff (dismissals.js, audit.js) — still reads only the older, weaker prohibition: dismissals.js:38 "Read the CURRENT tree at ${A.repo} (nothing else under .gbg/, never ~/.gbg/)"; audit.js:71 "FILES UNDER .gbg/ YOU MAY OPEN — exactly these, with Read, and nothing else under .gbg/ or ~/.gbg/" (a bare list + prohibition, no grep-scoping technique).
findings.why_it_matters: These scripts hand an agent with live Grep/Bash access instructions to read "the current tree"/"the source" broadly right next to a `.gbg/rounds/` tree that holds prior rounds' verdicts and findings — an answer key for the very task being re-run. The fix in hunt.js/panel.js exists because a bare textual prohibition is not enough for an agent wielding an unscoped `grep -r`: a single broad search silently sweeps in `.gbg/` content. This is not hypothetical — running this exact audit, a broad `grep -rn "caveats" .` (no `--glob` exclusion) surfaced verbatim excerpts from `.gbg/rounds/2026-09-09-check-docs-02/verdicts/*.json`, i.e. a prior round's answer key for the identical HOME_ORDER question this diff touches. audit.js and dismissals.js grant an agent the same unscoped power and were edited in this same diff without picking up the mitigation their sibling files received.
findings.description: This diff adds a concrete, actionable `--glob '!.gbg/**'` grep-scoping instruction to two workflow scripts (RULE.DOC.CLASS_SWEEP: "a flagged instance is a sample of a class; fix the class, not the line") but the class — every workflow script that grants broad tree-read access adjacent to `.gbg/` round data — has at least four other members, two of which (dismissals.js, audit.js) were touched in this identical diff for unrelated reasons and left with the older, weaker wording.
findings.evidence: hunt.js:74 "scope every grep with `--glob '!.gbg/**'`"; panel.js:88 "scope every search with `--glob '!.gbg/**'`"; dismissals.js:38 "Read the CURRENT tree at ${A.repo} (nothing else under .gbg/, never ~/.gbg/) and decide:"; audit.js:71 "FILES UNDER .gbg/ YOU MAY OPEN — exactly these, with Read, and nothing else under .gbg/ or ~/.gbg/:"

findings.title: New module-level glossary duplicates its own 'hat' definition verbatim, unlinked, in the one sibling site the same diff didn't sweep
locations: src/Witnesses.jl:13, src/CLI/RoundFiles.jl:7, src/CLI/Rounds.jl:9,128, src/CLI/Schema.jl:41-42, src/DocLints.jl:11-12, src/CLI/Gate.jl:15-16 (sibling terms correctly linked back)
findings.before: Preflight.jl's resolve_hats docstring (base) had no standalone sentence defining "hat" at all — it went straight from the arguments to "Each hat carries `key`; `substrate`, which view of the corpus...".
findings.after: This diff adds, verbatim, to Preflight.jl:200: "A hat is one persona of the `check-consistency` panel, reading the corpus from a single standpoint." — the identical sentence (module-glossary capitalisation aside) added as the canonical, "bound once here" definition of **hat** in src/GBGCodingTools.jl:20. Every other term the same new glossary defines (instrument, round, lane, Workflow) was, in this same diff, wired at its pre-existing explanation site to read "...(one of the four review procedures [`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) binds)" or "...bound in [`GBGCodingTools`](@ref)" instead of restating the definition — e.g. Witnesses.jl:13, RoundFiles.jl:7, Rounds.jl:9, Schema.jl:41-42, DocLints.jl:11-12, Gate.jl:15-16. "hat" is the one term in the new glossary whose only other explanation site got the same duplicate sentence with no backlink.
findings.why_it_matters: The package's own rule for this exact situation (RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED: "a term of art is defined in a clause or @ref-linked on first use") and its self-application discipline (this diff's own pattern, applied to every sibling term) is broken for the one instance it missed: a reader hitting Preflight.jl first sees a second, silently-duplicated 'canonical' definition with no pointer to the actual home, so the two copies can drift the next time either is edited — the exact failure RULE.DOC.CLASS_SWEEP exists to prevent, in the very diff that added a rule about rules needing checks.
findings.description: The diff establishes one canonical home for "hat" (and five sibling terms) in the module docstring and sweeps every other explanation site to @ref back to it — except the one other site (Preflight.jl:200) that states the identical sentence, which it added fresh in this same diff without the backlink the sibling terms all received.
findings.evidence: src/GBGCodingTools.jl:20 "A **hat** is one persona of the `check-consistency` panel, reading the corpus from a single standpoint."; src/CLI/Preflight.jl:200 "A hat is one persona of the `check-consistency` panel, reading the corpus from a single standpoint." (no @ref, no mention of GBGCodingTools); contrast src/CLI/Schema.jl:41-42 "A Workflow is the instrument's `workflow/*.js` script and a lane is one agent's share of the round it runs, both bound in [`GBGCodingTools`](@ref)."
